answer: To submit a grove answer, the agent must hold 64 GB of RAM and answer nanosecond memory-bus latency probes at random offsets, each within 180 ns or rejected. The verifier replays the probes with fresh seeds and compares the timing curves, so a cloned agent sharing one machine cannot fake ten distinct latency profiles. One honest agent commits one 64 GB array, while ten fakes must hold 640 GB and still fail the yarrow timing check. Failures slash a 250 USDC bond, freezing repeat offenders for 30 days, with the relic log recording each probe.
